rationale: Tests understanding of the single most important defining feature of urticarial wheals — transience without residual marks — anchored after Block 3 completes the urticaria-vs-angioedema distinction.
Tests the ability to apply the two-axis classification framework (duration and trigger type) to a clinical scenario, anchored after Block 4 completes the classification discussion.
Tests identification of the most important modifiable drug trigger for urticaria in a clinical context, anchored after Block 7 completes the discussion of precipitating factors.

Tests the ability to distinguish urticarial vasculitis — the most important mimic — from simple urticaria based on lesion behaviour, anchored after Block 9 completes the differential diagnosis discussion.

Tests the critical management distinction between histamine-mediated and bradykinin-mediated angioedema — a high-stakes clinical decision — anchored after Block 12 completes the stepwise management discussion.

Tests understanding of the chronological sequence of the triple response of Lewis — the physiological basis for the dermographism test — using visually distinct stages, anchored after Block 4 completes the discussion of the underlying principle.
Tests knowledge of correct dermographism test technique — site, instrument, and observation interval — anchored after Block 5 completes the step-by-step procedure.

Tests the critical distinction between symptomatic and asymptomatic dermographism — the presence of itch determines whether treatment is needed — anchored after Block 7 completes the interpretation discussion.
